Handing one over

The queue shows an owner. It could not change one, and coordination is where a multi-user product is actually judged.

Assigned2026-05-22 09:31 AWST

PFOS + PFHxS at MW05 — 37× the ANZG 2018 DGV

A. Nakamura → R. Whitmore — Environmental Lead · due 2026-05-22 17:00 AWST

A. Nakamura09:31

Confirmed against the certificate — both components detected well above the limit of reporting, so this is not a laboratory artefact. Handing to you for the condition 21 notification. The Contaminated Sites Act duty is open as well and is a separate lodgement.

R. Whitmore10:04

Acknowledged. Lodging condition 21 today. Raising the CS Act report with legal first — the wording commits us on the site’s status and that is not mine to draft alone.

A. Nakamura10:22

Understood. I have attached the certificate and the lineage export to this item so whatever goes out cites the same numbers.

The thread hangs off the exceedance rather than off a chat channel, so it is still attached in two years when somebody asks why the notification was worded the way it was.

Opening a result in another project switches your scope, and says so before it does.

Row-level security is fail-closed: you see MOCK-KRJ here because you hold a binding on it. Following that row moves the whole application into that project — the header changes, and so does what every other screen is about. A scope that changes silently is how somebody reads the wrong site’s numbers into a report.

When you hold no bindings at all

Fail-closed row-level security means real users meet this state — on their first day, and again the morning after a group membership is revoked. It cannot dead-end.

○ You are signed in, and you hold no project bindings.

Strataflow reads your access from your organisation’s directory groups, not from a list kept here — so nobody at Strataflow can grant it, and neither can this screen. Your administrator adds you to a group like SG-Strataflow-<project>-Contributors; access appears the next time you sign in. You are signed in as anakamura@wandalup.example on tenant wandalup.example.

A single-project customer never sees any of this

Most customers run one project. The switcher in the header collapses to the project name with no control on it, this screen is not linked from anywhere, and / lands on the project rather than here.

Switcher ceremony for a user with one thing to switch between is the kind of scaffolding that makes an internal tool feel like one. The URL still exists and still resolves; nothing in the architecture is special-cased, only what is shown.

This is not a dashboard

Every number here is a question somebody actually arrives with, and every one of them is a link to where it is answered. Nothing on this page exists to be looked at.

The distinction is load-bearing rather than stylistic: a decorative tile becomes stale without anybody noticing, because nobody was going to act on it. A tile that is the entrance to a queue is corrected the first morning it is wrong.

Groups, and what changing one touches

Groups drive criteria applicability, programme membership and figure series, so a membership change is never only a label.

Adding MW07 to “Compliance boundary” would change:

  • Locations reassigned3 bores move from TSF to Compliance boundary
  • Criteria applicability changesLicence Table 4 begins applying to 3 bores
  • Historical evaluations affected0 — applicability is resolved at evaluation date, not re-run
  • Programmes touchedGW-QTR keeps all 3; GW-MTH loses 3
  • Figures whose series would change4 saved figure configurations name an area

Reversible. Group membership is audited with before and after state, and applicability is resolved at evaluation date — so nothing already evaluated moves.

Survey history. A resurvey takes effect from its own epoch and moves nothing behind it; a correction supersedes and reaches back.
EpochKindTop of casingApplies toBy

Groundwater elevation is derived at the measurement date, never stored.

A depth-to-water reading taken in 2022 reduces through the 2019 datum; the same depth taken last week reduces through the 2024 one. Storing the elevation would freeze whichever datum happened to be in force the day it was calculated, and a resurvey would silently invalidate years of hydrograph.

Nest B — Borefield — this bore is half of a pair

MW03B is screened 46–52 m in the confined unit and MW01A 18–24 m in the superficial, at the same location. A register lists them as two rows; they are one installation, and the thing worth knowing is the difference between them.

The nest, read vertically.
BoreHydrostratigraphic unitScreened intervalStanding levelHeadEC
MW01ASuperficial18.0 – 24.0 m bgl11.42 m btoc203.40 m AHD840 µS/cm
MW03BConfined (Wandalup Sandstone)46.0 – 52.0 m bgl9.18 m btoc204.26 m AHD1120 µS/cm

Vertical gradient: Upward, +0.86 m from the confined unit to the superficial. The confined unit sits at higher head than the superficial one, so vertical leakage here is upward and TSF seepage in the superficial aquifer cannot be reaching the confined unit at this location. That is a containment argument, and it is only visible when the two bores are read as a nest rather than as two rows in a register.

Why this is not a footnote

A containment argument is made or lost on the vertical gradient, and it is invisible in every screen that treats a bore as a point. Two rows in a register, sorted alphabetically, with the number that matters being the difference between them.

Every QC sample names its parent by code. The incumbent alternative is a naming convention — MW05-DUP beside MW05, related by a substring and by nothing the database knows, and unrelated the moment somebody types MW05 DUP.

38 containers across 11 samples — the same 38 the chain of custody sealed on 14 May and the same 38 the laboratory reconciled on arrival (38 of 38). Three screens, one addition: a manifest that cannot be added up to the number on the custody form is the first thing a challenge finds.

MW11 is not on this manifest, and that is the finding rather than an omission.

The 2026 Q2 window closed on 14 May in Australia/Perth and the bore was not sampled — it is nine days overdue on the programme and short nine results on the data quality assessment. A manifest that quietly listed it, or that omitted the row without saying so, would let an overdue round read as collected.

The QC taxonomy, closed — and split by where each control is made

Every control this round rests on, what it is made from, and the question it answers.
ControlMadeThis roundParentWhat it answers
Field duplicate (blind)fieldWDL-26Q2-004
WDL-26Q2-008		WDL-26Q2-003
WDL-26Q2-005		Sampling and analysis together — the only control that carries the act of collecting
Field blankfieldWDL-26Q2-QC1The event itself — poured at MW05, at the boreContamination from handling and from the air at the bore
Trip blankfieldWDL-26Q2-QC2The cooler — travelled with the samples, 12–15 MayContamination picked up in transit, in the cooler, by the containers themselves
Equipment blank (rinsate)fieldWDL-26Q2-QC3Bladder pump, rinsed between WDL-26Q2-003 and WDL-26Q2-005Carry-over on equipment reused between two bores — the glossary’s equipment blank, and the rinsate a field officer asks for
Laboratory duplicatelaboratoryLD-268841WDL-26Q2-003Laboratory precision alone — the same bottle, split at the bench
Method blanklaboratoryMB-268841The preparation batchContamination introduced in preparation
Laboratory control samplelaboratoryLCS-268841A certified standardAccuracy against a known concentration
Matrix spikelaboratoryMS-268841WDL-26Q2-005Recovery in this water, not in clean water
Matrix spike duplicatelaboratoryMSD-268841WDL-26Q2-005Whether that recovery reproduces — it did, at 64%
Surrogate (isotope-labelled)laboratoryM8PFOSEvery PFAS samplePer-sample recovery on the PFAS suite

The split is the point. A field duplicate and a laboratory duplicate are both duplicates and they are not the same control: one carries the act of collecting and the other does not, so a pair that disagrees says something different depending on which it was. Products that list them under one word have thrown away the only thing the pair was collected to separate.

The bench controls belong to the laboratory batch, not to this round — a control sample applies to a batch, which is what makes “which results does this failed spike qualify” answerable. The matrix spike on WDL-26Q2-005 is the one that failed, and it qualifies every zinc result in PAS-WO-268841 rather than the sample it was made from.

No composites. FR-1.7’s depth intervals and increment traceability are soil and sediment work, staged S8 — every row above is a discrete grab, and drawing a composite here would be drawing a matrix the slice does not carry.

A blind duplicate stays blind, and the link is still recorded

Two field duplicates this round — WDL-26Q2-004 and WDL-26Q2-008 — and the laboratory was told about neither. The link exists in the record from the moment the sample was collected, so the RPD can be computed, and the laboratory never had the chance to make two results agree.

The distinction the screen has to keep is between the laboratory did not know and we do not know. Showing the parent here is correct; showing it on anything the laboratory receives is not.

QC linkage
WDL-26Q2-004 → parent WDL-26Q2-003 · MW05 · declared at collection 2026-05-13 08:40 AWST by A. Nakamura. Zinc RPD 38.2% against a 30% limit — open in QA/QC.

Commit — IMP-0239

Before — what the control says it will do

Committing IMP-0239 writes, in one transaction:

  • Results39
  • Derived results1
  • Lineage records40
  • Evaluations, across 2 criteria sets78
  • New exceedances raised2
  • Rows held rather than written3

Reversible. A committed run can be withdrawn, which removes its results from every register that counted them and leaves the reversal itself on the record — a reversal is an event, not an erasure.

The counts come from the staged data rather than from this screen, and they are the same numbers the receipt below will report. A commit control that does not say what it will write is asking for a signature on a blank page.

Held, and there is genuinely nothing to accept

Row 24held 5 days

Sulfate as SO₄ · MW09 · 2026-05-14

The laboratory reported −999, which their format defines as analysis aborted. That is not a concentration, and there is no value here to accept, qualify or estimate. Storing it as a number would invent a measurement; storing it as zero would invent a clean result.

No “accept anyway” — there is nothing to accept.

Most held rows have an answer. This one does not, and the screen says so rather than offering a control that would produce a lie. An interface that always offers a way forward teaches people to take it.

What the bore was doing before the sample was taken.

A sample is defensible because the parameters had stabilised, not because a number was written in a box.

A large disagreement between the two means the sample changed between the bore and the bench — degassing, a temperature artefact, or a mislabelled container — and it is worth catching before the whole suite is interpreted. It is a consistency check that costs nothing and nobody runs it.

The bore that did not stabilise, and what the record says

MW0914 readings · 22 L

Turbidity never fell below 10 NTU across 14 readings and 22 L purged.

Sampled anyway at the field officer’s judgement, and the record says so. Every metal result from this sample carries qualifier T — turbidity above the acceptance limit at collection — because a filtered metal from a turbid bore reads high and nobody can tell afterwards whether that was formation water or suspended sediment.

Qualifier T carried to every metal result

The field officer sampled anyway, which is the right call at a remote bore on a day rate — and the record makes it a stated judgement rather than an invisible one. A product that only accepts stabilised samples would simply have no record of this bore at all.

Custody is a chain, not a PDF

A signed form scanned into a folder proves a form was signed. It does not answer the question a challenge actually asks: was this sample ever unaccounted for.

Every transfer above is a row with a time, two parties and a seal number, so an unbroken chain is a query rather than somebody reading four pages of handwriting. The one exception in it is marked as an exception and carries forward to the result it affected.

Chain of custody — 2026-Q2-GW

Every hand that held these samples, from the bore to the laboratory bench.

a proposal — not in the product

Proposed. The PRD names no chain-of-custody surface, and there is no route for one.

FR-1.6 gets the samples as far as the event and FR-3.8 picks them up at the certificate; the days in between are where a defensibility argument is actually won or lost. Receipt and custody draws the laboratory end of the chain because that is where the record used to start — which is the tell. A chain reconstructed afterwards from a scanned form proves that a form was signed; it does not answer the question a challenge asks, which is whether these samples were ever unaccounted for. This screen argues for itself and is filed under Sampling events on that argument. It is called Chain of custody rather than eCOC because the glossary has an entry for custody transfer and none for the acronym: practitioners call the paper form a COC and the electronic one an eCOC, and both words are named here once rather than becoming the product’s (QB-9).

The rows are ordered by sequence rather than by time — two handovers can share a recorded minute, and a chain ordered only by the clock closes silently over a missing link. Here they run 1 to 7 with nothing missing between them, and that is the property worth having: a gap in the sequence is a hole somebody has to explain, where a gap in a list of timestamps is invisible. The last four rows are the ones Receipt and custody has always drawn — they are the same four rows, read from the same record, not a second copy of them.

Sealing a cooler and handing it over — what that writes, before you do it:

  • Transfers appended1 — appended, never edited
  • Containers committed to the consignment38 across 11 samples
  • Seal numbers frozen onto the transfer4471, 4472
  • Samples that can still be added to this chain0 — a sealed cooler is closed
  • Rows that can be corrected afterwards0 — a correction supersedes and both entries stay readable

Not reversible in the ordinary sense. A transfer cannot be edited or deleted; a mistake is corrected by a superseding entry that names what it corrects, and both stay on the record. That is what makes the chain evidence rather than a document.

One seal number, written down twice, differently

Seal number on the second cooler lid — the field record says 4472 and the laboratory’s receiving form says 4427.

Seal 4471 and the temperature check agree. Nothing about the containers is in doubt; the identity of one seal is. Both seals were found intact, which is a different check and it passed. The product has not chosen between the two numbers and will not: a transposition is the likeliest reading, and the likeliest reading is exactly what a custody challenge attacks.

Where this record stops, and what picks it up

This screen owns the chain: raising it in the field, the containers it accumulates, the seals, and every transfer up to and including the handover the laboratory signs for. It owns the discrepancy above, because a disagreement about a seal is a custody question.

Receipt and custody owns what the laboratory found when it opened the box — cooler temperature, preservation, breakages, holding time on arrival — and the results those explain. The cracked sulfate bottle is its finding, not this one’s.

After that the round leaves custody altogether and becomes a deliverable: the certificate and the rows that come back are Import runs. Three screens, one seam each, and each seam named on both sides of it.

What arrived, and in what conditionThe field round that filled it

A round with no chain yet

○ 2026-Q3-GW has no chain of custody, because it has not been collected.

There are 5 rounds on this project and 4 of them have one. This is the other: planned, with a window, a location list and an analyte suite, and no samples yet. That is a different sentence from no rounds have ever been sampled, and a screen printing “No data” for both would have said nothing in either case. The chain is raised at the first bore, on the device, before the first container is filled — not typed up afterwards from a notebook. Raising one writes an empty record attributed to you, and it can be discarded until the first transfer is signed.

An amendment on a round that has already been reported

PAS2026-01884 rev B re-reports 3 results on 2026-Q1-GW, and that round is inside a locked period.

The period 2025 Q1 – 2026 Q1 — locked, reported to DWER was closed to writes when the 2026 Q1 report went to DWER, and a locked period refuses a write rather than warning about one. The amended values are staged: computed, previewed, and standing nowhere. Nothing on the exceedance register, the TARP board or the licence has moved, and nothing will until somebody decides. Why the laboratory re-issued

Finding 1 — Calibration blank contamination — dissolved metals, ICP-MS run of 2026-02-10

The laboratory’s own quarterly review of its calibration records found the blank used to standardise positions 7 to 12 of batch PAS-WO-261188 carried copper and zinc above its acceptance limit. Copper and zinc on the samples in those positions were reported high. Nickel, cadmium and the major cations were unaffected — they were not in the contaminated blank.

Re-analysed on 2026-07-28 from the retained, acid-preserved aliquots. The samples were collected on 2026-02-04, so the re-analysis sits inside the six-month holding time for dissolved metals, which closes on 2026-08-04. Outside that window the amendment would not have been analytically defensible and the laboratory says so on the certificate.

Finding 2 — Dilution factor — EDTA hardness titration, same batch

The titration was performed at a 1-in-5 dilution, recorded as such on the bench sheet, and reported against a 1-in-4 factor. The reported hardness is 25% low.

No re-analysis: the titration reading is on the bench sheet and only the factor applied to it was wrong, so the correction is arithmetic and exact — 268 × 1.25 = 335 mg/L as CaCO₃.

On the numbering: Pilbara Analytical Services numbers a whole re-issue afresh and suffixes a partial one: PAS2026-04398 became PAS2026-04417 because every result on it was re-reported, and this one keeps its reference with a revision because three results on it did. Which document stands is a supersession either way.

The chain, hop by hop

  1. 1
    What the amendment changed3 results at MW05 re-reported — copper, zinc and total hardness. The supersession recordCopper 4.7 → 1.2 µg/L · zinc 18.2 → 4.6 µg/L · hardness 268 → 335 mg/L. Nothing is overwritten; the issued values stay readable beside the amended ones.
  2. 2
    Recalculated derivationsThe hardness cross-check reconciles for the first time, and 3 hardness-modified criteria at this bore are recomputed. How this criterion was calculated2.497 × Ca + 4.118 × Mg over the same calcium and magnesium — which were not re-analysed — gives 337.6 mg/L. Against the issued hardness that is −20.6%, outside the ±10% limit; against the amended one, −0.8%.
  3. 3
    Changed exceedance outcomes2 of 4 assessed outcomes change — both from exceedance to compliant. The exceedance registerCopper and zinc at MW05 in 2026-Q1-GW come off the register. Nickel and cadmium do not change although their criteria move, and the table below says why.
  4. 4
    Changed condition outcomes2 of 4 windowed series change, and the condition 12(c) trip is withdrawn. Licence L8842/2019/1The trip at 2026-Q1-GW is what raised the groundwater investigation programme lodged on 2026-02-27 — an obligation already discharged that would rest on a value no longer standing.
  5. 5
    Trigger states0 of 4 TARP levels move. The TARP boardLevel 2 holds on arsenic rather than on copper, so the monthly programme at MW05 holds with it. Each level is stated below with the reason it stays, because a trigger that is simply not mentioned reads as a trigger nobody checked.
  6. 6
    Affected reports1 of 4 issued submissions, and one item in the 2026 Q2 draft. Snapshot and regenerationQuarterly Groundwater Monitoring Report — 2026 Q1 was lodged on 2026-04-28 11:02 AWST against snapshot SNAP-0117. The lodged document does not change; what changes is whether the record still says what it said. Figure 5.1 in the draft figure list is already flagged stale on this.
  7. 7
    The decisionAccept, record as no material impact, or hold — and it is the decision, not the data, that is outstanding.The entire 2026 Q2 round is untouched: this certificate reports the February round, so nothing on the results crosstab moves either way.

The three results, and the two that did not move

As issued beside as amended. A superseded value is struck, never removed — a reader holding last quarter's printed report has to be able to find the number it contains.

Zinc is the row worth reading twice. Both the result and its criterion move, and they move in opposite directions — the amended hardness makes the criterion less strict, from 5.69 to 6.88 µg/L, while the amended result falls from 18.2 to 4.6. The outcome changes because the result moved further than the criterion did, and a screen that showed only one of the two would look like it had shown the working.

What the withdrawn trip reaches

Copper at MW05 tripped on 2026-Q1-GW, and that trip is what raised the groundwater investigation programme lodged with DWER on 2026-02-27. Accepting the amendment does not un-lodge it: a document that has gone to a regulator is withdrawn by writing to the regulator, and the product records which of those happened rather than doing the second one.

The 2026 Q2 exceedance register would also read differently. Copper at MW05 would read first rather than 4th consecutive quarter, and zinc first rather than 2nd consecutive quarter — the run column is counted from the rounds, so it moves when a round does.

The window and the criterion in force at each round are frozen onto the outcome. A licence varied next year re-evaluates future rounds and moves nothing already decided — the same rule the notification screen keeps about a deadline.

The two series that do not move, and why not

●holds Zinc (filtered) at MW07 — MW07 was analysed in a different position on the run and is not covered by either finding. Its values do not move, so its run does not.

●holds Electrical conductivity at MW05 — Electrical conductivity is read on a conductivity cell, not out of the metals digest. Neither finding reaches it.

Stating why a series did not change is the half of an impact preview that is usually left out, and it is the half a reader needs in order to trust the half that did.

The decision

Accept the amendment into a locked period, record it as no material impact, or hold it and ask the laboratory.

Accepting the amendment into a locked period would write:

  • Supersessions appended, with a reason on each3
  • Results whose value is replaced in place0 — a superseded value stays readable
  • Assessed outcomes recomputed4
  • Outcomes that change2
  • Windowed series re-evaluated4, of which 2 change
  • Licence conditions whose outcome moves1 — 12(c), from triggered to not triggered
  • Obligations already lodged that this puts in question1
  • Issued documents altered0 — a snapshot is what was issued
  • Snapshots flagged for reissue review1
  • 2026 Q2 results touched0

Accepting appends supersessions, and an appended supersession is never deleted. A decision made in error is corrected by a further supersession that names what it corrects, and both stay readable. What is reversible is the evaluation rather than the record: outcomes are recomputed from the values that stand, so a correction moves them back.

The ways out, each with what it writes

Three options and a refusal. None of them deletes anything, and none is the default (PP4, QB-7).
OptionWhat it does
Accept the amendmentWrites 3 supersessions against a locked period with the reason on each, re-evaluates 2026-Q1-GW, withdraws 2 exceedances, recomputes 2 window runs, withdraws the condition 12(c) trip, and flags snapshot SNAP-0117 and the 2026 Q2 draft as stale. It does not delete anything and it does not reissue anything: the reissue is its own decision, on its own screen.
Record as no material impactWrites a decision record with a stated reason and leaves the standing values where they are. The amended certificate stays attached to the round and findable. A blank reason is refused — “no impact” with nothing behind it is the judgement this record exists to hold.
Hold, and ask the laboratoryWrites a query against the certificate and nothing else. The amendment stays staged and the round stays locked. Use it where the re-analysis itself is in question rather than the arithmetic.

What is refused, and what cannot be undone

Refused: Replacing the three values in place. The period is locked because it has been reported to DWER, and a locked period refuses the write rather than warning about it — a number that has gone to a regulator is superseded with a reason or it is not changed.

Irreversible: Accepting appends supersessions, and an appended supersession is never deleted. A decision made in error is corrected by a further supersession that names what it corrects, and both stay readable. What is reversible is the evaluation rather than the record: outcomes are recomputed from the values that stand, so a correction moves them back.

Field capture — 2026 Q3 round

Water levels, field parameters and observations, recorded at the bore.

a proposal — not in the product

Proposed. Nothing in FR-1 to FR-8 covers field data capture.

U1 is named the highest-frequency user and every requirement in the PRD is about what happens after a laboratory has already reported. The water level, the purge volume, the field pH and the observation that a bore was dry are collected by hand and typed in later, or lost. This is the gap that most affects the user the PRD says uses the product most.

Today’s run

LocationSWL, m btocField pHEC, µS/cmPurge, LObservationState
MW05captured
MW07captured
MW09captured
MW11recorded as dry

Tab moves along the row, Enter drops to the next bore in the same column — because a round is entered column by column, one parameter at a time, not bore by bore. D marks a bore dry.

On a phone this grid stacks into one card per bore rather than panning. Everywhere else in this product a dense table pans with its identifying column frozen, which is right for a table you read — this one is typed into, standing at a bore, one-handed, and a grid that pans horizontally puts the column you are filling off the screen.

Open the purge log for MW05

Why a dry bore is a first-class record

A dry bore is not a missing reading. The hydrograph draws a gap rather than a line through it, the sampling programme reads the round as attempted rather than overdue, and the report says so. Left as an absence, all three of those go wrong quietly.

Offline by design: the site has no signal. Captured locally, queued, and synced when the vehicle reaches the gate — with the capture timestamp kept, not the sync timestamp.

Every check names the batch it ran in and the limit it was measured against.

A control sample applies to a laboratory batch, not to a sample — so “which results does this failed spike qualify” is answerable rather than a judgement call. And the acceptance limits are a versioned set with a stated source, because “why 30%?” is the same question a regulator asks about a criterion.

A reporting limit above the criterion is not a pass.

Cadmium was reported at <1.0 µg/L against an ANZG 2018 guideline value of 0.54 µg/L. Nothing was measured either way, so the outcome is indeterminate and it is drawn as its own mark. Recording that as compliance is the single most consequential error this product exists to prevent.

Spike against history — a finding with no limit behind it

Electrical conductivity at MW05 — 3410 µS/cm this round

Flagged against this bore’s own record, not against a fixed limit. Eleven rounds of rise and then a step: the trend explains part of this and not the size of it. The finding is raised, not resolved — whether it is a step change in the seepage plume or a sampling artefact is a question for the trend test and the purge record, and the product does not guess between them.

Laboratory batches

The unit QC is actually run on, and everything it qualifies.

/projects/:projectId/batches

A control sample applies to a batch, not to a sample.

Laboratories work in batches — a work order, prepared and analysed together — and one method blank, one control sample and one matrix spike cover all of them. Without the batch, “which results does this failed spike qualify?” has no answer, and a single failure either qualifies nothing or is applied to everything out of caution. Both are wrong.

Zinc matrix-spike recovery of 62% is below the 70% limit and it is reproducible across the duplicate, so this is matrix interference rather than a one-off. Every zinc result in this batch — nine samples, including the MW05 exceedance at 31.6 µg/L — is qualified as biased low. A recovery below 100% biasing low means the true value is likely higher, so the exceedance stands and is if anything understated.

A recovery below 100% is not simply “bad data”

The zinc spike recovered 62% of what was added, reproducibly across the duplicate. That is matrix interference — something in this water suppresses the measurement — and it means the reported zinc is biased low.

Which direction the bias runs is the whole finding. A result already above the guideline value, biased low, exceeds by at least the factor shown. The exceedance is strengthened, not weakened, and a screen that reported only “QC failed” would have left a practitioner to argue the opposite.

Zinc · MW05

Reported 31.6 µg/L against a criterion of 8.0 µg/L — 4.0×. Corrected for 62% recovery the true value is nearer 51 µg/L, or 6.4×. The reported value is used; the correction is stated and never silently applied, because a recovery-corrected number is an estimate and the certificate is a measurement.

Data quality objectives

The acceptance limits every QC check is measured against, and where each one comes from.

/projects/:projectId/objectives

A guideline value gets a version, an effective date and a source. A QC limit is the same kind of object and was not treated as one.

A regulator asking “why 30%?” is asking exactly the question they ask about a criterion. Hard-coding the answer means the product cannot say, and means a customer whose own data quality objectives are tighter has no way to apply them without a release.

The applicability rule is the part that was wrong

Relative percent difference near the limit of reporting

RPD is only meaningful when both results sit well above the reporting limit. A duplicate pair of 1.2 and 1.8 µg/L against a 1.0 µg/L limit gives an RPD of 40% and means nothing at all — the two numbers are the same measurement inside its own uncertainty.

Applying the 30% limit to every pair raises a failure on almost every near-limit duplicate, and a QC flag that is usually noise is a QC flag people stop reading. Above 5 × LOR the percentage applies; below it, an absolute difference of 2 × LOR does.

Zinc at MW05: 21.4 and 31.6 µg/L, both above 5 × LOR — the 38.2% failure is real

Changing a limit reaches forward only

Field duplicate RPD moved from 25% to 30% on 2025-07-01, and the 5 × LOR applicability rule was added in the same revision. Results evaluated before that date keep the limits in force then.

Tightening the field duplicate limit from 30% to 25% would:

  • Future pairs newly failing, on last year’s data4
  • Historical QC outcomes rewritten0
  • Reports already issued that would change0
  • New version created1 — 2026.1, effective on a date you choose

A limit is versioned with an effective date, exactly as a criteria set is. A result evaluated under 2025.2 keeps that verdict, and the version that produced it is on the result.

What “not met” actually costs

Not metConsequence for the assessment
Sensitivity — cadmiumCadmium cannot be assessed at any location. Seven results are reported as unassessable rather than compliant, and the recommendation is a method change from Q3.
Accuracy — zincNine zinc results are qualified biased low. The MW05 exceedance stands and is understated; no result is corrected.
Completeness — 87%Below the 95% objective. MW11 was not sampled and MW09 is two results short — one cracked container, one holding time. The round is reported as incomplete rather than as a clean 58 results.

Written before the round, not after it

The objectives on this page were set when the programme was designed. That ordering is the whole point: an assessment written after the results are in is an argument, and every practitioner who has read one knows the difference.

Where an objective was not met the product does not soften it, and does not quietly drop the dimension from the report. It states the shortfall, its consequence and the remedy — which is what makes the rest of the report credible.

Comparability — met

Arsenic’s reporting limit stepped from 5.0 to 1.0 µg/L in May 2025 on a method change. It is recorded, it is drawn as a stepped line on every plate that spans it, and the trend test treats the earlier censored values as censored rather than as measurements. A series whose limit changed silently mid-way is a trend nobody can defend.

MW05 — what the imbalance means

A −7.8% cation–anion balance says the anions exceed the cations by more than analytical error explains. On a bore whose sulfate is 918 mg/L, the likely readings are a sulfate result reported high, or a cation the suite does not include.

It is raised as a review item rather than resolved. The product does not know which, and guessing would be a silent derivation (PP3).

Condition 12(c) — three consecutive rounds, evaluated

Condition
L8842/2019/1 condition 12(c)
Rule
Three consecutive quarterly rounds above the criterion, at the same location, for the same parameter
Parameters and locations
Copper, zinc and electrical conductivity, at MW05, MW07, MW09 and MW11
What it obliges
Notify the CEO and lodge a groundwater investigation programme within 30 days of the third round being evaluated
Window
2025-Q3-GW → 2026-Q2-GW · 4 rounds
Evaluated
2026-05-21 14:06 AWST
Rule version
consecutive-window v2 · bound to Licence L8842/2019/1 v2024.2
One rule, four series, four outcomes.
LocationParameterCriterion2025-Q3-GW2025-Q4-GW2026-Q1-GW2026-Q2-GWRunOutcome
MW07Zinc (filtered)ANZG 2018 · 95% · 8.0 µg/L· 2.6· 3.1· 4.8▲ 9.41 of 3○not triggered
MW05Zinc (filtered)ANZG 2018 · 95% · 8.0 µg/L· 6.9· 7.4▲ 18.2▲ 31.62 of 3◐one round short
MW05Copper (filtered)ANZG 2018 · 95% · 1.4 µg/L▲ 2.1▲ 3.0▲ 4.7▲ 6.44 of 3■triggered
MW05Electrical conductivityLicence Table 4 · ≤ 2500 µS/cm· 2180· 2330▲ 2710▲ 34102 of 3◐one round short

▲ marks a round above the criterion and · one below it, so the run reads across the row without reading the numbers.

Twelve series are evaluated — three parameters at four bores. Eight have no round above the criterion anywhere in the window and are not drawn; a register of nothing happening is not a finding, and it would bury the four that are.

What each outcome did, in words

○not triggered Zinc (filtered) at MW07. The first round above the criterion at this bore. Two more consecutive rounds would oblige a notification; one round below resets the count to nothing.

The equipment blank taken after the pump was used at MW05 carries 1.4 µg/L of zinc, so carry-over cannot be ruled out on this result — a run that begins on a qualified result is worth watching rather than acting on.

◐one round short Zinc (filtered) at MW05. One round short. A third consecutive exceedance in 2026 Q3 trips the condition, and the monthly programme now running at this bore means that round arrives in weeks rather than in a quarter.

■triggered Copper (filtered) at MW05 — tripped on 2026-Q1-GW. Tripped on 2026-Q1-GW, which is the round the 30-day clock ran from. This round extends the run and raises nothing new — the obligation is the one already lodged, and the response it obliged is the TARP Level 2 escalation in force since 2026-03-01.

◐one round short Electrical conductivity at MW05. One round short, on the licence limit rather than a guideline value. The same four numbers are the tail of the record the QA/QC outlier check measured this round’s value against — one series, two questions, and they do not have the same answer.

Why the outcome is stored rather than re-computed

The window and the criterion in force at each round are frozen onto the outcome. A licence varied next year re-evaluates future rounds and moves nothing already decided — the same rule the notification screen keeps about a deadline.

The site’s own TARP is a second window over the same rounds and it is stricter — Level 2 escalates on two consecutive rounds, not three, which is why monthly sampling at MW05 has been running since March while the licence condition has tripped once. The two windows are drawn apart on purpose: the licence is what a regulator enforces and the TARP is what the site committed to, and a product that merges them loses which one was breached.

If the window were widened to five rounds, before anybody widened it:

  • Series whose outcome would change0 — a longer window cannot break a run that is already unbroken
  • Outcomes already decided1 — copper at MW05, frozen with the rule that decided it
  • Obligations that would be re-raised0
  • Rounds that would be re-evaluated9 — every round in the new window, on the criterion in force at each

Reversible, and nothing is written by the preview. A condition change re-evaluates forward; outcomes already frozen onto an obligation stay as they were decided.

What only the second layout shows

Arsenic, zinc, sulfate and hardness are all rising together, quarter on quarter, at one bore. No single round says that — every one of them is just a number against a limit.

And the cadmium row shows something a single round hides completely: the reporting limit stepped from 5.0 to 1.0 µg/L between Q3 and Q4 when the laboratory changed method. The Q3 cell is indeterminate against both criteria sets; the later ones only against ANZG. A series that silently mixed two reporting limits would read as an improvement.

Rising hardness is not a background detail

Hardness went from 244 to 412 mg/L over the same four quarters, and cadmium, nickel and zinc are all assessed against criteria computed from it.

So the criteria moved too. The zinc criterion was 5.4 µg/L in 2025 Q3 and is 8.0 µg/L now — the limit relaxed while the result climbed, and the exceedance factor understates the change. Nothing on a single-round grid could tell you that.

How the criterion is calculatedAgainst background

Everything true about a value is on the value.

A superseded reading keeps its old value struck through beside the new one. A quarantined reading stays visible in brackets on a hatched ground rather than vanishing. A non-detect keeps the laboratory’s own <LOR notation and is never rendered as a substituted number.

The column set is a saved view, not a rebuild

The monthly review is a recall. Which locations, which analytes, which period, which criteria sets — the whole question, named and shared, so two people asking for “the compliance boundary numbers” get the same rows.

Three limits, and they are not the same number.

The incumbents carry these separately too — this is parity, not a differentiator — and the bar is that they never collapse into one. An LOR is what the laboratory will report to; an MDL is what the method can distinguish from noise; a PQL is what it can quantify reliably. Evaluating against a criterion uses the LOR, and the other two stay on the record because a re-analysis argument is made from them.

Assessed against each criteria set

One row per criteria set, evaluated concurrently. There is no single verdict, because there is no single criterion.

The state that is not a pass

A non-detect at an LOR of 1.0 µg/L against a criterion of 0.54 µg/L means nothing was measured either way. The laboratory did not find cadmium above 1.0; the criterion sits below that; the result is silent about the criterion.

An incumbent renders this as compliant by default, and a documented support thread records exactly that happening — <0.60 against a 0.5 standard, flagged in the alert email and shown as a pass in the chemistry table until a non-default setting was enabled. Two surfaces of the same product disagreed, and the default was the wrong one.

Here it is its own state, identically on every surface that shows it: this page, the crosstab, the box plot, the summary table, the report and the Excel export.

How this criterion was calculated

A hardness-modified guideline value, and every input that produced it.

/projects/:projectId/hardness

A criterion that is a function of another result inherits everything true about that result.

Cadmium, nickel and zinc at this site are assessed against values computed from hardness. If the hardness is wrong — wrong sample, wrong date, derived rather than measured, or above the range the relationship is defined over — then three exceedances are wrong with it, and nothing on a conventional results screen would show you that.

The hardness this criterion used

Sample
WDL-26Q2-003 · MW05 · 2026-05-13
Reported hardness
412 mg/L as CaCO₃
How
Reported by the laboratory, not derived
Method
APHA 2340C — EDTA titration
Reporting limit
1 mg/L

Cross-checked against the major cations

InputValue
Calcium (filtered)96.4 mg/L
Magnesium (filtered)41.2 mg/L
Formula2.497 × Ca + 4.118 × Mg
Computed hardness410.3 mg/L as CaCO₃
Agreement●0.4% against the reported value — within the ±10% reconciliation limit

Reported and computed hardness agree, so the criterion below rests on a number two independent measurements support. Where they disagree by more than 10% the result is a review item, because the criterion inherits the error.

The relationship, and where it stops

criterion = base × (hardness ÷ 30) ^ slope, evaluated at the capped hardness of 400 mg/L as CaCO₃

Capped. Capped at 400 mg/L. ANZG does not extrapolate the hardness relationship above that, so the criterion is computed at the cap rather than at 412 — the conservative direction, and it is stated rather than silently applied.

What the cap costs, stated rather than hidden:

  • Measured hardness412 mg/L
  • Hardness used400 mg/L
  • Zinc criterion at 4128.19 µg/L
  • Zinc criterion at the cap8.00 µg/L
  • Outcomes that change0

The cap makes the criterion slightly stricter, never looser. Extrapolating the relationship past the range it was derived over would be the silent choice, and it would be the one that favours the operator.

Rule version hardness-modified-tv v3 · bound to ANZG 2018 2018.1 — bound to the criteria set, not to the instance.

What it produced, analyte by analyte

Base value, exponent, resulting criterion, and the result it was compared against.
AnalyteBase valueExponentCriterion hereResultOutcomeNote
Cadmium (filtered)0.2 µg/L at 30 mg/L0.890.54 µg/L< 1.0 µg/LindeterminateThe LOR sits above the criterion, so the hardness adjustment does not rescue it.
Nickel (filtered)11 µg/L at 30 mg/L0.8511 µg/L14.2 µg/LexceedanceExceeds at 1.3×.
Zinc (filtered)8.0 µg/L at 30 mg/L0.858.0 µg/L31.6 µg/LexceedanceExceeds at 4.0×, and the batch matrix spike says the true value may be higher.
Why this screen exists

If hardness were 120 mg/L rather than 400, the zinc criterion would be 2.8 µg/L rather than 8.0 and the exceedance factor would be 11× rather than 4.0×. A criterion that moves by a factor of three on another analyte’s result is not a footnote.

So the hardness result is not a supporting analyte on a crosstab. It is an input to three criteria, and it is treated here as what it is — with its own reconciliation, its own cross-check and its own place in the lineage of every value it governs.

Closing it is a purchasing decision, so the screen makes it one

Moving cadmium to ICP-MS/MS at a 0.1 µg/L reporting limit:

  • Results that become assessable7 per round
  • Additional cost per round$126
  • Additional cost per year$504
  • Criterion the new limit sits below0.54 µg/L — by 5.4×
  • Rounds of history this fixes0 — it reaches forward only

Nothing here changes a stored result. A method change from the next round is recorded as a comparability note on the plate, because a reporting limit that steps down mid-series is visible in every figure that spans the change.

What the report says

Generated into §3, and worded so a non-technical reader cannot mistake it for a clean result:

Report §3 — Data quality

Cadmium was reported by the laboratory at a limit of reporting of 1.0 µg/L. The applicable ANZG 2018 95% species protection guideline value at the measured hardness is 0.54 µg/L. The reporting limit therefore sits above the guideline value and cadmium could not be assessed against it at any location this round. These results are not reported as compliant. A method offering a limit of reporting of 0.1 µg/L is available and is recommended from 2026 Q3.

Compare the alternative, which is what a product that has no state for this produces: seven rows of 0.001 in a compliance column, and a reader with no way to know.

One finding against the approved grammar, recorded rather than fixed

The rainfall bars are drawn in the rule-strong grey, which measures 2.41:1 against the plate ground — below the 3:1 floor for a mark that carries data. The nearest value that passes is the not-evaluated mark grey at 3.02:1, which is already a token in this product rather than a new colour.

It has not been changed here. The grammar was approved on 20 August and the reference plates are an oracle; a rendering that quietly improves on the thing it is measured against is indistinguishable from a rendering that drifted from it. This is a revision for Jerry to accept or refuse, recorded where it can be seen.

If the revision is accepted:

  • Reference plates to re-render and re-approve3 of 12
  • Contrast against the plate ground2.41 → 3.02
  • Series the bars could now compete with0 — still lighter than every trace
  • Tokens invented0

Not urgent either way. The skill’s own rule is that a contrast warning obliges visible labels or a table view rather than a colour change, and the panel above is that relief. Darkening the bars would be the better fix; leaving them is defensible.

Hydrogeochemistry

Piper, Stiff and Schoeller — what kind of water this is.

/projects/:projectId/hydrochem

What the plate says

Every bore except MW05 is a calcium-bicarbonate water, tightly clustered — the natural signature of the Superficial aquifer here. MW05 is sulfate-dominated and four times the ionic strength.

That is the difference between a bore with a high arsenic result and a bore receiving TSF seepage, and it is the argument a hydrogeologist has to make in the report. The chemistry makes it; the exceedance register alone cannot.

Ionic balance at MW05 is −7.8%, outside the ±5% acceptance limit, and that is stated here rather than left on the QA/QC screen. A plate drawn from data that failed a consistency check should say so on its own face.

Statistics and trend

Censored-data methods and non-parametric trend tests.

/projects/:projectId/statistics

Seasonal Mann–Kendall, on a series that is seasonal

TestSpSen’s slopeVerdict
Mann–Kendall780.0031.77 µg/L per quarter■increasing
Seasonal Mann–Kendall (quarterly blocks)410.0211.52 µg/L per quarter■increasing

The hydrograph on this bore shows textbook wet-season recovery, so the series is seasonal and the plain test treats that structure as trend. Both agree here — the increase is real and survives deseasonalising — but the plain test overstates its significance, and on a shorter series it can manufacture one. Reporting only the plain result on a seasonal series is a defensible-looking answer to the wrong question.

Both are reported. Showing only the one with the smaller p-value would be choosing the answer.

How the two non-detects entered the trend test

Non-detects enter the test as tied values below every detected result, which is what Mann–Kendall’s statistic is built for — it compares ranks, not magnitudes. They are never substituted, and the two here fall below the lowest detection so no tie is ambiguous. Where a non-detect has a limit above a detected value the pair is indeterminate and is scored as a tie rather than guessed.

Never substituted

Half the limit of reporting is the common shortcut and it puts an invented number into a rank test. With an LOR that stepped from 5.0 to 1.0 µg/L mid-series, substitution would have manufactured a step change of 2 µg/L at the method change — a trend created by the laboratory changing instrument.

Why not a linear regression

Environmental series are not normal, are not evenly spaced, and contain values the laboratory reported only as “below something”. Ordinary least squares assumes away all three.

Mann-Kendall asks only whether later values tend to exceed earlier ones, which is the question, and Sen’s slope gives a rate that a single outlier cannot swing.

Below n = 8 the test is reported with a sample-size warning and no p-value, rather than a number that looks like evidence.

Background comparison

Downgradient against reference, and where a site-specific trigger value comes from.

/projects/:projectId/background

At a mine this is the assessment, and a guideline value alone does not make it.

A default guideline value answers “is this water safe”. Background answers “did we cause it”, which is the question a licence condition and a closure argument both turn on. Where no default exists — sulfate has none — background is the only criterion available.

Reference population
MW12 (background) and MW01A, MW03B (upgradient) · 14 quarterly rounds each · 2023-01 to 2026-05
Method
ANZG 2018 §3.1.4 — site-specific trigger value as the 80th percentile of the reference distribution, applied where a default guideline value is absent or demonstrably unrepresentative.
Reference distribution against the downgradient bore, per analyte.
AnalyteBackground median80th percentileDefault guidelineTrigger adoptedMW05VerdictBasis
Sulfate as SO₄112 mg/L148 mg/Lnone — no ANZG DGV148 mg/L918 mg/L6.2× the site-specific triggerDerived — no default exists
Electrical conductivity890 µS/cm1,140 µS/cmLicence ≤ 2500 µS/cm1,140 µS/cm3,410 µS/cm3.0× background, 1.4× the licence limitBoth apply; the licence governs compliance
Arsenic (filtered)2.1 µg/L3.4 µg/LANZG 13 µg/Lnot adopted28.4 µg/L8.4× background, 2.2× the DGVDGV applies — a default exists and is representative
Total hardness128 mg/L166 mg/L—not a criterion412 mg/L2.5× backgroundContext for the hardness-modified values

What the pattern says

Every parameter elevated at MW05 is elevated against background as well as against a guideline, and the signature — sulfate, EC and hardness together — is TSF seepage rather than natural variation. Two bores upgradient in the same unit show none of it.

The signature

Sulfate 6.2×, electrical conductivity 3.0× and hardness 2.5× above background, together, at one bore in a line of seven. Two bores upgradient in the same hydrostratigraphic unit show none of it, and the nested confined bore is at higher head so it is not coming from below.

Any one of those numbers is arguable. The four together, with the flow direction, are not.

See it on the Piper plateFlow direction

Deriving the trigger honestly

The 80th percentile is computed over 42 reference results with two censored, using Kaplan–Meier rather than substitution. A site-specific trigger value derived by substituting half the limit of reporting would sit lower and manufacture exceedances.

Adopting the sulfate trigger at 148 mg/L as a criteria set:

  • Reference results behind it42
  • Censored, carried by Kaplan–Meier2
  • Locations it would apply to4 downgradient
  • New exceedances this round1 — MW05
  • Historical evaluations rewritten0

It becomes a versioned criteria set like any other, with the reference population and the date it was derived recorded on it — so a regulator can see which fourteen rounds of which three bores produced the number, years later.

STY01Reference2025 wet855Bathynellidae sp. B04, Candonidae sp. C11●persisting
STY02Downgradient2025 wet628Bathynellidae sp. B04 — 9 individuals●persisting

What it appears to say

Taxa richness at STY02 has fallen from 6 to 4 and individual counts from 28 to 12 across two events, while the reference bore held steady. The salinity and sulfate rise at MW05 sits between the two. This is the receptor the water-quality exceedances are ultimately about, and it is assessed on population persistence rather than against a concentration.

Two bores, two events

Taxa richness at the downgradient bore has fallen while the reference held steady, and the salinity and sulfate rise at MW05 sits geographically between them. That is a coherent story and it is not yet evidence.

Background comparisonFlow direction

And why the product will not draw a trend through it

Two events is not a trend. Stygofauna counts vary by an order of magnitude with season, haul effort and operator, and the honest reading is that this warrants a targeted survey rather than a conclusion. The screen says so rather than drawing a line through two points.

Everywhere else in this product a series of numbers gets a trend test. Here it does not, and the refusal is the design: counts that vary by an order of magnitude with season, haul effort and operator do not support one, and a Mann–Kendall drawn across four points would look exactly as authoritative as the arsenic plate that is built on fourteen.

◐ Two events. A trend needs more, and the product says so instead of drawing one.

The screen states what changed and recommends a targeted survey. It does not compute a rate, because a rate here would be a number with a confidence interval that nothing in the sampling design supports — and it would be quoted back for years.

Map

The monitoring network, symbolised by this round’s outcome.

/projects/:projectId/map

Which way the water goes

Every location on this project carries a position — upgradient, downgradient of TSF, compliance boundary — and until this plate those were attributes somebody typed. This derives them.

The surface is a planar least-squares fit through the eight superficial bores. That is the honest method for eight points: it states one gradient and one direction and cannot invent local structure the data does not support. Interpolating a curved surface through eight wells draws detail nobody measured, and it is the picture that gets argued with.

The network geometry decides whether this figure is possible at all. Six of these bores sit almost on one line, and a plane fitted through collinear points is barely constrained across that line — the first version of this plate returned a flow direction of due south on a site whose every other screen says south-east, with a residual of 1.46 m against its own one-metre limit. Two bores genuinely off the transect fixed it. That is why the residual is printed on the plate rather than kept in a log: it is the figure telling you whether to believe it.

MW03B is excluded. It screens the confined unit. Contouring two aquifers as one surface is the commonest error on a plate like this, and it produces a flow direction that is an average of two systems and true of neither.

What it confirms

Flow runs from the north-west to the east-south-east at about 2 m/km, on a largest residual of 0.04 m — a planar surface fits this network almost exactly. The TSF sits upgradient of MW05 and MW07, which sit upgradient of the compliance boundary at MW09 and MW11. The stored positions are correct — and now they are derived rather than asserted, so a resurvey or a new bore changes the plate rather than leaving a stale string on a record.

Symbology

Worst outcome per location across every criteria set. A bore compliant against the licence and above an ANZG guideline value reads as an exceedance, because that is the more consequential of the two.

Shape, not colour. The print layout is the same map at A3 with a north arrow, a bar scale, a grid and a title block — and it survives a monochrome office printer, which is where most of them end up.

GDA2020 is not WGS84. They agree only at epoch 2020.0 and separate by about 7 cm a year, so a WGS84 export carries its epoch and a conversion without one is refused rather than assumed.

A failing comparison blocks the snapshot, not the draft. Writing continues; issuing does not — which is the only point in the loop where the check is worth anything.

What a comparison is for

Every other check in this product measures the document against a rule — a unit is present, a reference resolves. This one measures it against an approved copy, which is the only way to catch a change nobody thought to write a rule about.

The reference is an oracle: it is approved once, by a person, and the assembled document is compared to it. Changing the reference and the document that asserts against it in the same act would make the comparison agree with itself, which is the failure mode of every golden test ever written in a hurry.

One row per check. What the reference expects, what the assembled document carries, and whether they agree.

The snapshot cannot be taken while §6 and §7 are unwritten.

Both failures are the same failure: the prescribed form requires an authored section and the document has 0 words in §6 and 0 words in §7. Nothing is wrong with the generated content — the crosstab, the registers and the figures all match the reference. The report is a draft, and the gate is saying so at the one moment it is worth saying: the moment somebody tries to issue it.

Write §6What a snapshot would captureWriting continues either way. Only issuing is blocked.

What a failure that is not an unfinished draft looks like — 2026-08-19 16:40 AWST

§3.2 — QA/QC summary table. The golden reference carries seven columns and the assembled table carried six: Action taken was dropped when the QA/QC generator changed.

Nothing in the document looked wrong. Every check that reads the document’s own structure passed, and a reader who had never seen the reference would have found §3.2 unremarkable — which is exactly why the comparison is against an approved copy rather than against a rule.

The generator was corrected and §3.2 regenerated the same afternoon. The failing run is kept; a gate with no record of what it caught is indistinguishable from one that has never fired.

Decide the amendment first

A number this document does not carry

Every cross-reference is checked against the numbers the document actually carries, and 18 of them resolve. A reference to Figure 4.9 would not: §4 carries 6 figures, and a reference past the end of a section is a finding rather than a rendering that quietly prints the literal text.

This is the check that costs nothing and that nobody runs. A dangling cross-reference survives every proofread, because the sentence around it reads perfectly well.

Adding Copper at MW05 across four rounds after Figure 4.2 makes it Figure 4.3. The copper series is what the staged amendment turns on, and §5.3 asserts a trip that a reader cannot check without seeing four rounds beside each other.

Interpretation — §6

Where the hydrogeologist writes, with the evidence beside them.

a proposal — not in the product

Proposed. FR-7 generates a report but nothing authors one.

FR-7.1 to FR-7.6 cover templates, numbering, snapshots and branding — the mechanics of assembly. A monitoring report is roughly half interpretive prose, and nothing in the requirement set says where that prose is written. Today the answer is Word, which reintroduces exactly the round trip QB-2 exists to remove.

6.1 Groundwater quality at MW05

Arsenic at MW05 was reported at 28.4 µg/L, above the ANZG 2018 95% species protection guideline value of 13 µg/L and the third consecutive quarter above that value [Figure 4.2].

Mann-Kendall over fourteen quarterly rounds reports a significant increasing trend (p = 0.003) with a Sen’s slope of 1.7 µg/L per quarter [Figure 4.6]. The major-ion signature at MW05 is sulfate-dominated and distinct from the calcium-bicarbonate background of every other bore [Figure 4.3], which is consistent with TSF seepage rather than natural variation.

Cadmium could not be assessed at any location this round: the laboratory’s limit of reporting of 1.0 µg/L sits above the guideline value of 0.54 µg/L

Evidence to hand

Every citation is a live reference. If Figure 4.6 is regenerated, the number in the sentence is flagged — not silently updated, because a sentence somebody wrote is theirs.

The unfinished sentence is the point. A practitioner writing about cadmium needs the indeterminate outcome in front of them, not in another tab.

7 differences across 4 sections, from 3 amended results — which is the ratio worth noticing. Three numbers move and seven things in the document change, because a monitoring report says the same result in several places and each of them is a place a hand-edit misses.

The issued artifact is immutable, and that is not the same claim as “nothing has changed”.

The bytes lodged with DWER on 2026-04-28 are held and reproducible; no amendment, no re-evaluation and no configuration change reaches them. What can change is the record they were drawn from, and the two columns above keep those apart so that “what did you report” and “what do you now believe” are separately answerable years later.

Reissuing

Reissuing the 2026 Q1 report would write:

  • New snapshot taken1 — SNAP-0124, with its own digest
  • Results it would stand on228 — 3 at amended values
  • Sign-offs required again3 — prepared, reviewed, approved
  • The issued document SNAP-01170 changes — it is what was lodged and stays so
  • Submission record1 new · the accepted 2026 Q1 submission is superseded, not replaced
  • Sections needing an author before it can go1 — §6.1 cites a trip that would no longer stand

A reissue is reversible up to lodgement and not after: the new snapshot can be discarded while it is a draft, and a document that has gone to DWER is withdrawn by writing to DWER. The product records which of those happened; it cannot do the second one for you.

Not available while the amendment is staged. A reissue that regenerated against values nobody has accepted would put an undecided number into a regulatory submission. The control is drawn and refuses, rather than being absent: somebody deciding the amendment upstairs needs to see what a reissue costs before they decide, not after.

A monitoring period is resolved in the site’s own timezone, never the server’s.

A quarterly round at a Pilbara bore begins at 16:00 UTC on 31 December. A sample collected at 08:00 on 1 April local time belongs to the June quarter — get it wrong and the round it was meant to satisfy reads as missed while a spurious extra one reads as satisfied.

MW11 is nine days overdue and has been alerted on and escalated. The round is not marked complete while a location is outstanding — a programme that reads as satisfied with a bore missing is worse than one that reads as nothing at all.

MW05 is on two programmes, and a screen showing one of them would be wrong.

GW-QTR runs quarterly across the network. GW-MTH runs monthly at MW05 and MW07, and has since 2026-03-01, because a TARP Level 2 trigger required increased frequency — so MW05 is next due on 2026-06-14, not 2026-08-14. A programme that read as satisfied while a monthly round went uncollected is the two-surfaces-disagree failure this product exists to end, and it is the escalated round that gets missed because it is the one nobody planned for.

A frequency raised by a trigger comes back down by a decision

GW-MTH exists because the data crossed a line, and it does not lapse when the data recrosses it. Standing it down is a decision somebody makes and signs, against the TARP’s own stand-down condition — four consecutive rounds below the trigger — because a monitoring frequency that relaxed itself the first quiet quarter is the one that misses the next event.

Standing GW-MTH down would:

  • Rounds removed from the calendar8 per year
  • Consecutive rounds below trigger required4 — currently 0
  • TARP level this would return MW05 toLevel 1
  • Historical rounds affected0

The control is present and refuses, rather than absent. An operator who cannot see what would release them from a monitoring burden cannot plan against it.

Statutory notification

A countdown against a window, from a timestamp nobody can move.

Why this timestamp is immutable

Window and rule frozen onto the event at 2026-05-22 09:14. A later licence variation cannot move this deadline.

A statutory notification window runs from “became aware”. Missing it is an offence rather than a service failure, so the database refuses an update that moves that timestamp — or the obligation link, because the two together are what the countdown was computed from.

“As soon as practicable” is stored as a null window and read as owed now, never as a blank. The countdown invents no number, and time remaining is truncated rather than rounded — 4 h 59 m never displays as 5 h.

One moment of awareness, two statutory duties, two parts of the regulator.

The licence condition is not the only thing with a clock. The Contaminated Sites Act imposes its own duty on becoming aware of known or suspected contamination — a separate instrument, a separate branch of DWER, a separate lodgement — running from the same timestamp. Discharging one does not discharge the other, and the two are routinely conflated because most products model only the duty written into the licence.

Recording that it is with legal discharges nothing. The clock keeps running and the record says so.

Approval and sign-off

Who approved exactly what, and when.

/projects/:projectId/signoff

Sign-off is not a validation state.

Validation says the data is right, and it is made result by result. Approval says a named person accepts responsibility for a document, and it is made once. Collapsing the two means either that approving five hundred results signed a report nobody read, or that signing a report silently approved five hundred numbers.

6signatures held
4documents signed
1awaiting
3staged changes under a signed snapshot
One row per signature, not per document. A signature names the capacity it was given in and the digest of what it covers.

The top row has no digest and that is the honest state, not a gap: the 2026 Q2 report has no snapshot, so there is nothing to sign. A signature offered against “the current draft” would bind to whatever the draft became afterwards. The golden comparison blocks the snapshot, the snapshot is what a signature binds to, and the order is not incidental.

Three signatures, in three capacities, all dated before the document went out: prepared A. Nakamura 2026-04-24 15:40 · reviewed D. Okafor 2026-04-27 09:18 · approved R. Whitmore 2026-04-27 16:12. A signature dated after lodgement would be a signature on something already gone.

The amendment does not reach it

The staged amendment re-reports 3 results that SNAP-0117 stands on. It changes nothing about this approval. The snapshot is append-only, its digest is unchanged, and the document R. Whitmore signed regenerates from it byte for byte.

That is the reason a signature binds to a snapshot rather than to a project, a period or a query. Bound to any of those, an amendment eighteen months later would silently change what a named person is on record as having accepted — and the person would be the last to know.

What is true, and is stated rather than left to be noticed: 3 of the 228 results beneath this signature have an amended value staged against them. The signature stands; the agreement between the signed document and the standing record is what would move, and it is the “against today’s record” column that carries it.

Superseding a signature is not a thing this product offers. A signature is withdrawn by a further signed act that names it, and both stay readable.

What a new approval would cover

If the amendment were accepted and the 2026 Q1 report reissued, the approval requested would cover:

  • A new snapshot, with its own digestSNAP-0124
  • Results it would stand on228 — 3 at amended values
  • Capacities required again3 — prepared, reviewed, approved
  • Exceedances the document would report7 for the period, down 2
  • The approval of 2026-04-270 changes — it covers SNAP-0117 and continues to
  • Sections needing an author first1 — §6.1 cites a trip that would no longer stand

A requested approval can be withdrawn before it is given. Once given it is a record of what somebody accepted at a moment, and it is never edited — a mistaken approval is answered by a further signed act that names it.

Project settings

What this project is, what it evaluates against, and who can act in it.

/projects/:projectId/settings

What a “project” is for a single-operator customer is not settled, and this screen cannot be finished until it is.

Facility-coextensive — one project per site, always — or a work scope inside a facility, so a closure study and routine compliance monitoring are separate projects over the same bores? The first is simpler and matches every fixture. The second is what a consultancy would need, and the authorisation model already supports it. The screen is drawn against the first reading and says so, rather than quietly choosing.

Identity

Appears in the header, in every export filename and on every report cover. Changing it does not change the URL, which is a UUID.

The facility supplies the area hierarchy every location hangs from.

Every monitoring period, due date and countdown resolves here and never on the server. A quarterly round at a Pilbara bore begins at 16:00 UTC on 31 December — get this wrong and a round that was satisfied reads as missed while a spurious one reads as met.

GDA2020 and WGS84 agree only at epoch 2020.0 and separate by about 7 cm a year. A WGS84 coordinate carries its epoch; one arriving without an epoch is refused rather than assumed.

Reversible. Binding a set evaluates forward and re-evaluates on demand; it never rewrites an outcome that has been reported.

Reporting calendar

The month a reporting year ends. With June, 2026 Q1 is July–September 2025 — a fiscal quarter is not a calendar quarter, and a calendar year is not a special case of this, only the December setting.

PFAS is assessed here against ANZG, and ANZG is not the operative PFAS framework

The PFAS National Environmental Management Plan is the agreed ANZ position. It carries its own values, its own derived sums and — the part that matters — a value per receptor, because what protects freshwater ecology is not what protects a drinking-water supply.

Criteria setVersionProtectsPFOS + PFHxSState
PFAS NEMP — freshwater 95%2.0Aquatic ecosystems0.13 µg/Lavailable
PFAS NEMP — drinking water2.0Human health, potable0.07 µg/Lavailable
PFAS NEMP — recreational2.0Human health, contact0.7 µg/Lavailable
ANZG 2018 — 95%2018.1Aquatic ecosystems0.13 µg/Lactive

Assessing against ANZG alone is defensible for freshwater ecology and insufficient the moment a potable or recreational receptor sits downgradient. Because evaluation here is concurrent and every set is versioned, carrying all three is a content decision rather than an architectural one — which is exactly the kind of thing a customer should be able to do without calling anybody.

Applicability

A criteria set is bound by matrix, location group, hydrostratigraphic unit, analyte, fraction and period — not by a global switch. Two sets apply to MW05 concurrently and both outcomes are kept.

G8 promises the customer’s own team can do this without an implementation consultant. Today it is a seed file, and this screen is what that promise actually requires.

Non-detect rule is bound to the set, not to the instance

Regulators specify different rules, and the derived total can cross a criterion depending on which applied. A global setting would make one of the two answers silently wrong (FR-2.2). The workspace below runs that choice against the record rather than describing it.

The non-detect rule, run over the record it decides

PFOS + PFHxS · derived by sum-pfas-anzg v2.1 · limit of reporting 2.0 ng/L on each component · criterion 0.13 ng/L (ANZG 2018 · 95%).

Bound to the set

What a non-detect contributes to a derived sum

There is deliberately no default, in the schema or in the code. A criteria set without a rule cannot be stored, because the alternative is a value that looks like a decision and is not.

In force: exclude from the sum. Changing it here changes it for this set only — the Licence Table 4 set keeps half-limit substitution, and both answers are kept because two regulators asked two questions.

Why this is a criteria-set field and not a setting

Zero is the dangerous one. Under it every censored total becomes 0.0 ng/L and six results that nobody could assess read as compliant. Nothing on the page would look wrong. That is the same failure as a reporting limit above a criterion rendering as a pass, arriving through a different door.

Under the limit of reporting the same six read as exceedances at 31×, which would raise six statutory notification obligations. One field, and the round is either quiet or a compliance event.

Which is why it is bound to the set: a regulator that specifies half-limit substitution and a regulator that specifies exclusion are both answerable at once, and neither answer is a global preference somebody changed on a Tuesday.

A version pair, one field apart

ANZG 2018 — 95% species protection — 2018.1 in force, 2026.1 in draft. The version is this instance’s configuration of the set, not a new edition of the guideline: no value in it moves.

Activation, and what it starts

Activating version 2026.1 on 2026-09-01 → if activated would write:

  • Criteria set versions written1 — 2018.1 is superseded, not deleted
  • Derived totals re-evaluated7
  • Outcomes that change6 — indeterminate becomes exceedance
  • Exceedances raised6, at six locations
  • Notification obligations raised under condition 216 — became-aware set at activation, immutable
  • TARP levels that extend automatically0 — Level 3 names MW05 and extending it is a separate decision
  • Locked periods re-evaluated0 — a rule change evaluates forward
  • Issued reports changed0 — a snapshot is what was issued

Reversible as an evaluation and not as a consequence. Rolling back re-evaluates the seven totals and withdraws the six exceedances; it does not un-lodge a notification that has gone to DWER.

Why activating a criteria set is an approval, not a save

Condition 21 obliges notification as soon as practicable on becoming aware of an exceedance, and the moment of awareness would be this activation. Six statutory clocks, started by a configuration change and running from a timestamp nobody can afterwards move. That is why activating a criteria set is an approval rather than a save.

A became-aware timestamp is immutable at the database and a statutory window runs from it. Missing that window is an offence rather than a service failure — so a configuration change that manufactures six of them belongs behind the same named approval a submission does.

Nothing here re-opens a locked period. The 2026 Q1 round is closed, and a rule change evaluates forward — which is the opposite of the staged amendment, where the data moved under a period already reported and the write has to be decided.

Rollback

Rolling back to version 2018.1 would write:

  • Set version deactivated1 — superseded, and both stay readable
  • Derived totals re-evaluated7
  • Exceedances withdrawn6 — withdrawn, never deleted
  • Notifications un-lodged0 — a lodgement is withdrawn by writing to the regulator
  • Audit records writtenOne per change, appended, attributed

Reversible as an evaluation. An exceedance withdrawn by a rollback is withdrawn and not deleted, and it stays readable with the version that raised it and the version that withdrew it.

What rollback cannot undo

Rollback is drawn as a control rather than left to a database restore, because the question it answers — “we activated the wrong rule on Friday” — is asked on a Monday by somebody who is not a DBA.

A lodged notification is not a row this product owns. It is a document with a regulator, and it is withdrawn by writing to the regulator. Rolling back the rule withdraws the exceedance that obliged it and records that the notification stands — a product that quietly cleared both would have deleted the evidence that a notification was made.

The vocabulary maps inward, never outward

ESdat calls it EQL. The domain calls it LOR, and so does every screen, every column heading and every report label in this product.

A format that leaked its own vocabulary into the application would put two words for one concept in front of a practitioner, and the glossary guard fails the build for exactly that.

A mapping that was learned wrong, and the correction

Corrected 2025-02-0331 results re-derived

TDS (calc) was mapped to Total dissolved solids (dried) for six months. The laboratory calculates this from electrical conductivity and does not dry it, so every result carried a method it was never measured by.

Correcting the mapping did not edit the results. It superseded them: 31 new results, each pointing at the one it replaced, each carrying the rule version that produced it. The originals are still readable, still attributed, and still show what a report issued in that window was based on.

See the supersession cascadeOpen lineage on one

Correcting Cd-diss → Cadmium (total) would touch:

  • Results re-derived and superseded44
  • Evaluations recomputed88 — two criteria sets
  • Outcomes that would change3
  • Reports already issued that cite them2 — flagged stale, not rewritten
  • Original results deleted0

Reversible as a further correction. Nothing is overwritten — a correction supersedes and reaches back, and the reports that cited the old values stay exactly as they were issued, marked stale.

Never asked twice — but never hidden either

There are three outcomes on a review question, not two, and conflating the last two would put decisions into somebody’s history that they never made.

OutcomeWhose decisionShown as
OutstandingNobody yet — it blocks the commitA question in the queue
Applied from a prior decisionA named person, on a named importApplied, with their name and the import it was made on
Applied by the dictionaryNobody — it is a synonym, not a judgementApplied, attributed to the dictionary

The middle row is the one that has to keep its attribution. “The system did it” and “you did it, eighteen months ago, on the Kurrajong import” are different answers to an auditor, and only one of them is true.
